Are you passionate about finding technology solutions for drug development, so our scientists can focus on the science?

Do you have experience with IT product discovery and continuous development?

If so, now is your chance to join Ascendis Pharma as our new IT Product Owner for the Scientific Solutions team.

Ascendis Pharma is a global biopharmaceutical company committed to making a meaningful difference in patients’ lives. Guided by our core values of Patients, Science, and Passion, we are applying our innovative TransCon® technology platform to fulfill our mission of developing new therapies that demonstrate best-in-class potential to address unmet medical needs.

At our headquarters in Hellerup, Denmark, research facilities in Heidelberg, Germany, and additional offices across Europe and the United States, we are advancing programs in our Endocrinology Rare Disease and Oncology portfolios. We also collaborate with partners on the development of TransCon-based products in other therapeutic areas and markets.

Our context

This position is based in our Global IT organization. Over the past five years, we have built and matured a product-driven organization with a strong focus on product management and lifecycle thinking. Our long-lived teams take ownership from problem discovery through solution delivery and continuous improvement, ensuring that we address real business needs.

Our structure combines clear leadership intent with empowered teams. Each team member is supported by a People Leader focused on development and a Functional Leader guiding strategy and delivery. We foster autonomy and self-organization to enable fast flow, clear accountability, and minimal dependencies.

The Scientific Solutions team supports Product Innovation, Product Development, CMC, Nonclinical Development, and Global Medical business functions. Across these areas, the common objective is to identify and develop technology solutions that enable pharmaceutical product innovation.

We are seeking a passionate IT Product Owner to join our growing Scientific Solutions team. As a key member of Global IT, you will play a crucial role in shaping coherent technology offerings across applications, tools, and data for a broad scientific user group.

This is an exciting opportunity to work in a fast-paced environment and collaborate with cross-functional, global teams to achieve extraordinary results.

You will report to Jakob Monajemzadeh Thrane, People Leader in Global IT, and, from a functional perspective to Ivanna Rosendal, Global Head of Digitalization. The position is based at our headquarters in Hellerup, Denmark.

Your key responsibilities will be:

• Ensure that a broad scientific user group has coherent technology offerings across applications, tools, and data that evolve with their needs.

• Communicate closely and frequently with users and leadership teams to create a clear, shared understanding of the most important needs and priorities.

• Translate business needs into technology deliverables and coordinate with relevant IT teams to ensure prioritization and completion.

• Prioritize and manage the Scientific Solutions team’s backlog and actively help remove impediments to technology delivery.

• Collaborate closely with other teams across Global IT to manage dependencies and align priorities.

Qualifications and skills:

You hold a relevant academic degree, at minimum a master’s degree, and have 5+ years of experience in a related role within a pharmaceutical, biotechnology, or comparable scientific environment.

Furthermore, you have:

• A background that enables you to understand the translational stage of drug development.

• Hands-on experience managing and developing a technology product portfolio.

• Experience with product discovery and decision facilitation.

• Experience driving the successful delivery of digital products and platforms.

• Experience working in an agile team and continuously improving ways of working.

Key competencies:

You are a strong team player, innovative and curious, and have a can-do attitude.

You possess an entrepreneurial mindset and can thrive in an informal, open environment where innovation and change are key.

To succeed in this role, we also expect you to be a proactive self-starter who can identify opportunities for improvement and take initiative to move things forward.

Our team needs to scale to support the ever-growing demands, so we need team members who both can act pragmatically, and solution orientated for the short term, and at the same time are able to think long-term to ensure what we do today can grow to support us in the future.

Travel: 10-25 days per year

Office: Tuborg Boulevard 12, 2900 Hellerup

Apply now!

We evaluate applications as they are received, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible. Please note that we conduct interviews on a rolling basis and reserve the right to remove the job posting at any time.

To ensure your application is reviewed, please submit it through the specified platform. Applications sent by email or through other channels will not be evaluated.

You can learn more about Ascendis Pharma by visiting www.ascendispharma.com.

We’re looking for a product engineer to help us build better tools for legal research. You’ll work mainly on the backend, with a say in what we build and responsibility for taking it from an early idea to something customers use every day. That includes asking whether we’re solving the right problem, deciding what’s worth shipping first, and knowing when something needs more time.

About Pandektes

Our mission is to rebuild legal research from the ground up. Lawyers still lose countless hours to fragmented sources, outdated systems, and databases that fight them at every turn. We're building the largest AI-powered legal database in the world to make that friction disappear.

We're a team of 40+ based in our Copenhagen HQ, Zurich, London, and Hamburg. We’re a small team with high trust and flat structure. We move fast, argue our positions, and ship. If your input is good, it gets implemented - often within hours, not sprints.

We have has raised more than €4M, including a €2.9M seed round (Feb 2025) led by People Ventures, Interface Capital, and a strong bench of angels. We already serve 400+ customers across Denmark, Germany, and Switzerland, and we're just getting started.

What we value

“How fast can we ship this?” comes up a lot at Pandektes. So does “we should take our time with this one.”

Knowing which question to ask is a big part of being an engineer here.

Knowing when it’s good enough

We like getting things into customers’ hands quickly. That means making trade-offs, questioning scope, and accepting when something is good enough for now. There’s usually another approach to explore or another prompt to try. At some point, you have to ship.

We use AI throughout our development process. AI code reviews, feature flags, and remote coding agents running end-to-end tests help us move quickly with confidence. Deciding what to build, what to check, and when it’s ready still takes judgment.

We value people who can find a smaller version worth shipping, explain the trade-offs, and follow through once customers start using it.

Knowing when to slow down

Some decisions deserve more time. Getting them right makes everything that follows easier. Getting them wrong means paying for the same mistake repeatedly.

Our default is to move quickly, so slowing down takes discipline. Sometimes it means pushing back when the rest of us want to get something out. We value someone who can explain why the extra work matters, challenge an approach, and help us decide where to spend our time.

You’ll have room to make those calls here, and teammates who will question them. We expect you to do the same for us.

Make time to experiment

We enjoy trying things before we know whether they’ll work. A new tool, a different way to use an agent, an idea that might turn out to be useless. Finding out is part of the work.

Once a month, we get together to demo our setups, show what we’re experimenting with, and share what we’ve learned. Sometimes we invite people from outside the team to show us how they work. Those sessions have changed how we build software.

We value curiosity and the generosity to bring other people along. If you find something useful, show us. If an experiment fails, we’d like to hear about that too.

We try to watch this video once a month to keep this value top of mind.

The experience you’ll bring

You’ve built and operated backend systems that real customers depend on. You can work through questions about data, APIs, performance, and security, and explain the consequences of your decisions.

Our stack includes TypeScript, NestJS, GraphQL, Postgres, and Prisma. We also work with OpenAI and Turbopuffer. Experience with these tools is useful; we’re especially interested in what you’ve built with them and the decisions you made along the way.

You enjoy working through a product problem while it’s still taking shape. You ask questions, share unfinished work, and help decide what’s worth building. You’re comfortable taking a feature from those early conversations through implementation, testing, and delivery.

What we offer

You’ll join at a point where there’s still a lot to shape. We offer competitive pay and equity so you can share in the success you help create.

We are usually office based but we all work from home time to time. You’ll have your own Pleo card for the tools and work expenses you need, plus 25 vacation days a year, public holidays, and paid parental leave when your family grows.

We also make time to get together away from our usual work. Our last team trip was to Barcelona, and we’d love to have you along for the next one.

Pandektes is an equal opportunity employer

We believe diverse teams build better products and stronger teams. We embrace and encourage people from all backgrounds to apply regardless of race/ethnicity, colour, religion, nationality, gender, sex, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, socio-economic status, culture or beliefs.

Legal professionals should be able to stand behind every answer. We build the foundation for that: verified legal data, complete across time and traceable to its source, with research tools built for confident legal judgment. Our vision is clear: to be the leading platform for legal information retrieval, enabling in-depth and accurate legal knowledge in a fast, efficient and user-friendly way using artificial intelligence.

jobs.description:
The Department of Mechanical and Production Engineering (MPE) at Aarhus University is consolidating its research and teaching activities within the field of Design and Manufacturing and invites applications for a Tenure Track Assistant Professor/Associate Professor within the field of design and manufacturing from July 1st, 2027 or as soon as possible.

The MPE Department seeks an innovative and visionary researcher capable of establishing and leading an internationally recognized research group and delivering research-based teaching at the Bachelor, Master & PhD levels. The chosen candidate is expected to establish effective and visible research programs, develop local and international research collaborations, attract external funding, and contribute to our mechanical engineering bachelor and master programs with teaching at an international level

We welcome candidates with interdisciplinary research backgrounds who can help realize our vision of creating lasting impact by guiding the shift toward a resilient and sustainable industry, society, and planet.

For this open position, we are seeking candidates to advance research in resilient and sustainable design of products and manufacturing solutions.

We prefer candidates that can demonstrate the potential for industrial application of their research. The candidate should bridge existing fields in the section and department, and we encourage applicants to address potential synergies in our educational programs and research activities.

The selected candidate will be required to teach relevant courses in the MPE educational program at the B.Sc., M.Sc., and PhD levels of the Mechanical and Production Engineering programs. 

Expected start date 
July 1st, 2027, or as soon as possible.

To meet expectations in this role, we expect the candidate to fulfill the following requirements:
To meet expectations in this role, we expect the candidate to fulfill the following requirements:
- PhD or equivalent in Mechanical or Production Engineering or a closely related subject area.
- Substantial experience conducting high-quality research in the field of Sustainable Design and Manufacturing with publications in leading international journals that match career stage.
- Familiarity with experimental, computational, or theoretical research method.
- Interest in and prior experience with interdisciplinary collaboration across engineering disciplines and with industry is desired.
- For the position as associate professor, the applicants should, in addition, have:
- Documented teaching experience and a clear commitment to teaching and advancing mechanical engineering courses within the field of Sustainable Design and Manufacturing, from introductory undergraduate instruction through master’s and PhD-level study
- Documented record of self-directed research leadership, external funding acquisition, supervision of PhD students, and teaching and course development at university level.
- The candidate should have proficient communication skills in English.
- It is an advantage if the candidate has the ability or is willing to develop their communication skills in Danish.

Who we are
The engineering field in Aarhus University is evolving with a rapid growth in student population, major research initiatives as well as through the establishment of a number of new physical facilities in the city center of Aarhus. We have comprehensive plans for increased activities in research and education, as well as public and industrial cooperation. The Department of Mechanical and Production Engineering within the Faculty of Technical Sciences has cooperation with universities and advisory service providers in more than 20 countries. The engineering field at Aarhus University is well established with extensive research activities, over 700 mechanical engineering students and a long tradition of industrial cooperation that we wish to extend significantly.

What we offer 
The department offers:
- research infrastructure, laboratories and access to shared equipment 
- an exciting interdisciplinary environment with many national, international and industrial collaborators
- a research climate encouraging lively, open and critical discussion within and across different fields of research
- a work environment with close working relationships, networking and social activities
- a workplace characterized by professionalism, equality and a healthy work-life balance 

Place of work and area of employment 
The place of employment is Aarhus University, and the place of work is Mechanical and Production Engineering, Katrinebjergvej 89, DK-8200 Aarhus N, Denmark.

Contact information
For more information about the position contact Deputy Head of Department for Research Charles Møller (charles@mpe.au.dk / +45 61677786) or Head of Section Ramin Aghababaei ( ra@mpe.au.dk / +45 93508956)

Deadline
Applications must be received no later than January 4th 2027.

Technical Sciences Tenure Track
Aarhus University offers talented scientists from around the world attractive career perspectives via the Technical Sciences Tenure Track Programme. Highly qualified candidates are appointed as Assistant Professors for a period of six years with the prospect of performance- based advancement to a tenured Associate Professorship. 

The aim of the Technical Sciences Tenure Track Programme is to:

• attract outstanding talented individuals that are competitive at an international level
• to promote the early development of independent research success early in the career of scientists
• to create transparency in the academic career path
As part of the tenure track position, the candidate is offered:

• access to research infrastructure
• capability development, including postgraduate teacher training
• a mentoring programme
• support to develop scientific networks and to secure interdisciplinary research at the highest level
As part of the Aarhus University Tenure Track Programme, the University carries out a mid-way evaluation to review the progress of the tenure track candidate after three years, according to the same criteria used in the final tenure review. The final tenure review is conducted after five and a half years. If the review is positive, the candidate will be offered a tenured position as Associate Professor at Aarhus University.

Please refer to the tenure track guidelines for the tenure review criteria and for the tenure review process.

Application procedure
Shortlisting is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the assessment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. The selection is made on the basis of an assessment of who of the candidates are most relevant considering the requirements of the advertisement. All applicants will be notified within 6 weeks whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee and will receive his/her assessment. 

Formalities and salary range
Technical Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation. 

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

Research activities will be evaluated in relation to actual research time. Thus, we encourage applicants to specify periods of leave without research activities, in order to be able to subtract these periods from the span of the scientific career during the evaluation of scientific productivity.

Aarhus University offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including relocation service and career counselling to expat partners. Read more here. Please find more information about entering and working in Denmark here.

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.

The Environmental Microbiology Section at the Department of Environmental Science is currently looking for a VIP at the Associate Professor level who works on microbial degradation of pollutants in different environments who can provide novel dimensions, interpretation and project opportunities within contaminant microbial ecology. The new Associate Professor should also be able to interact and collaborate both within the department but also across the faculty with special emphasis on microbial ecology in industrial water.

Expected start date and duration of employment

1 April 2027 or as soon possible.

This is a permanent position.

We are especially interested in individuals whose research integrates microbial ecology under different redox potentials and thus can understand contaminant degradation processes in all elements of natural and engineered water systems from groundwater sediment to wastewater. Research focused on understanding the link between different omics techniques is particularly relevant here.

Applicants should have demonstrated experience in microbial ecology under different redox conditions and have a strong background in molecular microbiology and method development. Experience in defining and executing projects that involve water stakeholders is essential. Proficiency in a range of laboratory techniques, such as anaerobic culturing, pure culture characterization, antibiotic resistance genes and of metagenomic and meta-transcriptomic analysis, is desirable to fully utilize the analytical platforms available at Aarhus University (Risø campus).

Your models might start in Python. Their impact goes far beyond it.

Your career in data science might only just be getting started. At NORDEN, you will apply it to real logistics challenges involving vessels, ports, terminals, weather and cargo flows.

At NORDEN, moving cargo from A to B involves vessels, ports, terminals, weather, cargo flows and countless operational constraints. Understanding how all those pieces interact can make a real difference to the decisions we make and at the end our base margin.

As our new Data Scientist in Maritime Logistics, you will turn that complexity into models we can explore, test and learn from, helping us make better operational and commercial decisions.

You do not need years of experience or deep shipping knowledge. What matters is a strong foundation in Python and supply chains and the curiosity to apply it to the real world.

Why this role?

Because you get to take problems that exist in the real world and build models that help us understand what could happen next.

You might be modelling how vessels move through a logistics network, exploring the capacity of a terminal or testing what happens when weather, congestion or operational constraints change. Other times, you could be looking at historical data, improving an existing model or helping colleagues understand what different scenarios could mean commercially and operationally.

A central part of your role will be translating complex logistics systems into simulations that allow us to ask better questions before decisions are made in the real world.

You will work closely with commercial and operational colleagues while learning from experienced colleagues within analytics and shipping. Our broader Quantitative Analytics environment works with Python and technologies including Prefect, Docker and Azure and you will also gain practical experience developing solutions and visualisations using Power BI.

What you will be doing

You will work where shipping, logistics and data science meet. Helping us continuously improve how we work with simulation, optimisation, analytics and software development.

To be more specific you will:

• Design and develop simulation models of supply chains and maritime logistics operations.

• Use discrete-event simulation and agent-based modelling to represent vessels, terminals, ports and other parts of complex logistics systems.

• Analyse logistics networks and explore opportunities to improve capacity, throughput, utilisation and operational efficiency.

• Use historical and operational data to calibrate, validate and continuously improve your models.

• Build analytical tools that allow colleagues to explore scenarios and understand their operational and commercial implications.

• Develop robust analytical models and simulation solutions in Python.

• Create visualisations that make complex outputs easier to understand and use.

What you bring

There is no need to understand every aspect of shipping or every modelling method from day one. What matters is that you have a good analytical foundation, an understanding of supply chains and logistics and the curiosity to keep learning.

Qualification we are looking for:

• Have 0–3 years of relevant professional experience.

• Hold a degree in Supply Chain Management and Logistics, industrial engineering, operations research or another relevant quantitative field.

• Have a good foundation in Python and are comfortable writing structured, maintainable analytical code.

• Are fluent in English, our working language.

jobs.occupation: Professor / Associate Professor / Senior Researcher taking lead in Catchment and Freshwater Ecosystem sciences
jobs.description:
Are you an engaged, leading scientist of international standing, with deep expertise in the research of catchments and freshwater ecosystems, and excellent science leadership skills? Do you have the scientific vision to guide the strategic direction for a nationally and internationally recognized research community working with catchments, wetlands, lakes, streams and nature-based solutions?

The Department of Ecoscience at Aarhus University invites applications for a full-time permanent scientific position (Full Professor, Associate Professor, or Senior Researcher) in the Catchment science and Freshwater Ecology (CaFE) focus area. We are looking for a scientist who enjoys taking lead and working strategically with organizational impact covering the range of research areas in CaFE.

Expected start date and duration of employment

This is a permanent position from 1 April 2027 or as soon as possible.

Job description

The position centers around research and research based advisory in catchment processes and freshwater ecosystems – including wetlands, streams and lakes and the landscapes like forests, agricultural areas etc. that surround them.  We expect the candidates to have expertise and track record with one or more of the key thematic areas:

• Hydrology and the retention and transport of nutrients and hazardous substances

• Biogeochemical processes and emissions of greenhouse gases from land and water bodies, including interactions with carbon and nutrient dynamics

• Freshwater ecology and the links between abiotic and biotic processes, including ecosystem functioning, biodiversity, and responses to human pressures and climate change

• Nature-based solutions and ecosystem restoration to strengthen biodiversity and resilience and reduce nutrient loss, limit greenhouse gas emissions and regulate water flow in the landscape

• Combining long-term monitoring data with novel research using laboratory, mesocosm and field experiments, in situ sensor data and catchment- and ecosystem modelling

At Department of Ecoscience, all scientific staff in general are expected to contribute to external income generation, dissemination of knowledge, and talent development. Your specific scientific responsibilities may also include:

• Taking the lead on the development and implementation of the CaFE focus area strategy as part of the Department’s strategy, Ecoscience 2030 – including formulating concrete goals and action plans for implementation in dialogue with colleagues and the Department’s management

• Setting the direction and fostering a strong and inclusive research environment across the Section for Catchment Science and Environmental Management, the Section for Freshwater Ecology and the Centre for Nature-based Solutions

• Bringing our research and knowledge to Danish ministries and agencies as well as to other relevant national, European and international decision makers through science-based advice, making an impact for the society around us

• Promoting innovation within the focus area and wider department by fostering use of new and/or novel technologies through closer dialogue and interaction with other sections/focus area within the department and across the faculty

• Supporting the scientific development and career paths of colleagues in the focus area

Your profile

We are looking for a scientist with a strong research track record as well as documented experience with science-based advisory work and leadership of research staff. You have expertise within catchment science and freshwater ecology, previous experience working in interdisciplinary teams and from broad sectoral collaborations. Applicants must hold a PhD in hydrology, limnology, freshwater ecology, biogeochemistry, environmental science, physical geography, environmental engineering or a closely related discipline. The level of appointment (Full Professor, Associate Professor or Senior Researcher) will be determined based on qualifications.

We value in particular:

• Excellent leadership experience from similar research environments; e.g., leading larger research groups and taking responsibility for strategic development of larger units (academic citizenship)

• Skills in strategic scientific coordination, strategy development, project management, and building research networks

• An established international network, collaborative skills and relationships within catchment science and/or freshwater ecology and nature-based solutions

• Documented experience in securing and leading externally funded research projects

• Documented experience with science-based advisory work and engagement with authorities and other stakeholders

Excellent written and spoken English; Strong Danish language skills are an advantage.

Who we are

The Department of Ecoscience, with approximately 300 employees in Aarhus and Roskilde, is one of Denmark's leading research environments in applied ecology, spanning terrestrial, freshwater, marine, and Arctic ecosystems. We conduct both fundamental and applied research and deliver Science-based advisory services to authorities in Denmark and Greenland. Our work is grounded in long-term monitoring, field-based data collection, and advanced modelling, and we pride ourselves on a research culture characterized by high scientific integrity, strong interdisciplinary collaboration, and societal relevance. Our values are impact, professionalism, curiosity, collaboration and trust.

CaFE is the department's focus area for catchment science and freshwater ecology, integrating the Section for Catchment Science and Environmental Management, the Section for Freshwater Ecology and the Centre for Nature-based Solutions. We are around 80 research and technical employees working to generate the data and knowledge that qualify decision-making on conservation and recovery of deteriorated wetlands and inland waters. Our vision is to maintain and expand our position as the key national focal point for applied research and modelling within catchment processes and freshwater ecosystem dynamics, helping authorities monitor, manage and mitigate human impacts on wetlands and freshwaters.

We combine long-term monitoring data with experimental approaches and modelling, and we have the strongest national scientific environment within modelling of nutrient transport, biogeochemical processes in wetlands, experimental freshwater ecology, lake ecosystem modelling and lake restoration. Key infrastructure includes a series of living labs in constructed wetlands, lakes, ponds and streams, including the semi-field mesocosm lake experiments at Lemming that have been running for more than 30 years.

Find out more about our current strategy, departmental values and more here: https://ecos.au.dk/en/about-us/au-ecoscience-our-strategy

What we offer

• A full-time permanent scientific position with an internationally competitive research environment and access to unique long-term datasets and world-class field and semi-field infrastructure

• A central role in shaping the scientific direction of CaFE, contributing actively to the focus area strategy under Ecoscience 2030 and beyond

• An interdisciplinary and dynamic working environment across catchment, freshwater, terrestrial, marine and Arctic research

• Highly engaged, motivated and positive colleagues and an innovative and dynamic working environment, where culture and values are important

• A working environment characterized by high scientific standards, trust, and well-being

• Close, trust-based relationships with Danish ministries and agencies and strong national and international research networks

• Access to professional support for international researchers and their families relocating to Denmark

For candidates with the right qualifications and experience in strategic research leadership, a temporary role as Deputy Head of Department with responsibility for the CaFE focus area of the Department of Ecoscience will be possible. This role includes participation in the Department’s management group. Further education/competence building in leadership will be offered. Contact the Head of Department (details below) for a more detailed description of this role.

Place of work and area of employment

The place of work is AU Campus Aarhus, and the area of employment is Aarhus University with related departments.

Contact information

For further information about the position, please contact Head of Department Mikkel Tamstorf (mpt@ecos.au.dk; +45 53 57 50 44).

Application procedure

Shortlisting is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the assessment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. The selection is made on the basis of an assessment of who of the candidates are most relevant considering the requirements of the advertisement. All applicants will be notified within 6 weeks whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee and will receive his/her assessment.

Formalities and salary range

Technical Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation.

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

Research activities will be evaluated in relation to actual research time. Thus, we encourage applicants to specify periods of leave without research activities, in order to be able to subtract these periods from the span of the scientific career during the evaluation of scientific productivity.

Aarhus University offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including relocation service and career counselling to expat partners. Read more here. Please find more information about entering and working in Denmark here.

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.

• Have a proven ability to set strategic direction and lead complex initiatives across multiple teams and stakeholder groups.
